tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact:
Ladder (cost per GB descending): Express One Zone > Standard > Intelligent-Tiering > Standard-IA > One Zone-IA > Glacier Instant > Glacier Flexible > Deep Archive.
Min storage duration: Standard 0 / IT 0 / IA 30 / OZ-IA 30 / GIR 90 / GFR 90 / GDA 180 days. Min billable object 128 KB for IA classes; IT does not auto-tier objects <128 KB.
Retrieval: everything down to Glacier Instant = milliseconds. GFR: Expedited 1-5 min, Standard 3-5 h, Bulk 5-12 h (Bulk free). GDA: Standard 12 h, Bulk 48 h.
Lifecycle: objects must sit 30 days in Standard before transitioning to IA/OZ-IA; transitions only go DOWN the ladder (never IA -> Standard). Expiration deletes; noncurrent-version rules need versioning.
One Zone-IA = single AZ -> only for re-creatable data. Intelligent-Tiering = unknown/changing access pattern (monitoring fee per object, no retrieval fee).
Durability 99.999999999% (11 nines) all classes; availability 99.99 Standard, 99.9 IA, 99.5 OZ-IA.

tier_s_must_memorize_cold.topic: EBS / EFS / FSx / instance store picker
tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact:
EBS = one instance, one AZ, block. gp3 baseline 3,000 IOPS + 125 MB/s (max 16k / 1,000 MB/s, independent of size); gp2 3 IOPS/GB. io2 Block Express up to 256k IOPS, 64 TiB, sub-ms. st1 throughput HDD 500 MB/s (logs, big data); sc1 cold 250 MB/s; HDD cannot boot. Multi-Attach io1/io2 only, up to 16 Nitro instances same AZ.
EFS = shared POSIX NFS for Linux, Regional (multi-AZ) or One Zone, thousands of clients, ~3x EBS $/GB; classes Standard / IA / Archive with lifecycle; throughput Bursting / Provisioned / Elastic; performance General Purpose vs Max I/O. Not Windows.
FSx for Windows = SMB + NTFS + Active Directory + DFS, Multi-AZ. FSx for Lustre = HPC / ML, 100s GB/s, sub-ms, S3-linked (lazy load + export), scratch vs persistent. FSx for NetApp ONTAP = multi-protocol NFS+SMB+iSCSI, snapshots, SnapMirror migration from NetApp. FSx for OpenZFS = NFS, ZFS snapshots/clones, up to 1M IOPS, migrate ZFS/Linux file servers.
Instance store = ephemeral NVMe physically attached, millions of IOPS, lost on stop/terminate; scratch, buffers, replicated caches only.
S3 = object, HTTP API, static assets, data lake; not a POSIX file system (Mountpoint is read-mostly).

tier_s_must_memorize_cold.topic: RDS Multi-AZ vs read replica vs Aurora
tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact:
Multi-AZ (instance) = SYNCHRONOUS standby in another AZ, NOT readable, auto failover 60-120 s via DNS CNAME flip, same Region only, backups taken from standby. It is HA, not scaling.
Multi-AZ DB cluster = 1 writer + 2 READABLE standbys, semi-sync, failover <35 s (MySQL/PostgreSQL only).
Read replica = ASYNCHRONOUS, readable, up to 15 (MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL; 5 for Oracle/SQL Server), same or cross-Region, own endpoint, manually promotable (DR), can itself be Multi-AZ. No automatic failover.
Encryption: only at creation. Encrypt an existing DB: snapshot -> copy snapshot with KMS key -> restore. Replicas of an encrypted primary are encrypted.
Backups: automated 0-35 days (default 7), PITR to any second; manual snapshots persist until deleted; snapshots restore to a NEW endpoint.
Aurora: storage 6 copies across 3 AZs, self-healing, grows 10 GB -> 128 TiB; up to 15 replicas that double as failover targets (priority tier 0-15); writer + reader endpoints; failover ~30 s; Global Database = 1 primary + secondary Regions, <1 s lag, RPO ~1 s, RTO <1 min; Serverless v2 scales in 0.5 ACU steps; Backtrack rewinds MySQL up to 72 h with no restore; cloning is copy-on-write.
RDS Proxy: connection pooling (Lambda bursts), IAM auth, cuts failover time up to 66%.

Key-value/document, single-digit ms, serverless, horizontal. Item max 400 KB. RCU = 1 strongly-consistent 4 KB read/s (or 2 eventually consistent); WCU = 1 KB write/s. Transactions cost 2x.
Capacity: Provisioned (+ auto scaling, reserved capacity for steady) vs On-Demand (unpredictable/spiky, pay per request, ~5-7x unit price). Standard-IA table class for cold tables.
DAX = in-memory, in-VPC, API-compatible read cache, microsecond latency, for read-heavy/hot items -> NOT ElastiCache (that is for RDS). Hot partition -> fix the partition key (high cardinality, write sharding), not more RCUs.
Global tables = multi-Region ACTIVE-ACTIVE, needs Streams; last-writer-wins. Streams = 24 h ordered change log -> Lambda triggers; Kinesis Data Streams for DynamoDB = up to 365 days.
TTL = free background expiry (no WCU). PITR 35 days; on-demand backups; export to S3 (no RCU).
GSI = any partition/sort key, own capacity, eventually consistent, add any time (GSI throttling throttles the base table). LSI = same partition key + alternate sort key, create at table creation only, 10 GB per partition key, strongly consistent reads.
Read DynamoDB when: no joins, schema flexible, millions of TPS, serverless; pick RDS/Aurora when relational joins/ACID across many tables.

SQS Standard = decouple + buffer, unlimited TPS, at-least-once, best-effort order. FIFO = exactly-once + ordering per message group, 300 msg/s (3,000 batched), dedup ID 5-min window. Both: 256 KB (Extended Client Library -> S3 for bigger), retention 1 min-14 days (default 4), visibility timeout default 30 s max 12 h, long polling <=20 s, delay <=15 min, DLQ + redrive. Scale ASG on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible per instance.
SNS = push pub/sub, fan-out to SQS/Lambda/HTTP/email/SMS/Firehose, message filtering, FIFO topic -> FIFO queue. Pattern: SNS -> multiple SQS = durable fan-out.
EventBridge = event bus with rules; 100+ SaaS partners, cross-account buses, schedules (cron/rate), archive + replay, schema registry, content-based filtering. Pick for SaaS/cross-account/scheduled/routing on content.
Kinesis Data Streams = real-time, ordered per shard, REPLAY (24 h default, up to 365 days), shard 1 MB/s or 1,000 rec/s in, 2 MB/s out (enhanced fan-out 2 MB/s per consumer), record 1 MB; consumers: Lambda, KCL, Flink, Firehose. On-demand mode exists.
Firehose = near-real-time (buffer 60-900 s / 1-128 MB) delivery to S3/Redshift/OpenSearch/Splunk/HTTP, no storage, no replay, optional Lambda transform, Parquet/ORC conversion, zero admin.
Managed Service for Apache Flink (ex Kinesis Data Analytics) = SQL/Flink over streams. MSK = Kafka. Amazon MQ = lift-and-shift ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ (AMQP/MQTT/JMS). Step Functions = orchestration/workflow with retries (Standard 1 yr exactly-once; Express 5 min at-least-once, high volume). SWF = legacy.

Simple (one record, random if multiple values, no health check). Weighted (0-255 split, A/B, canary; weight 0 = stop). Latency (lowest RTT Region). Failover (active-passive; primary needs health check). Geolocation (WHERE user is: compliance/localized content; set a default). Geoproximity (bias +/- to shift traffic; needs Traffic Flow). Multivalue answer (up to 8 healthy records, client-side LB with health checks; not a load balancer). IP-based (by client CIDR).
Alias = free, zone apex OK, targets ELB/CloudFront/S3 website/API GW/Global Accelerator/VPC endpoint/another record in same zone; NOT an EC2 IP. CNAME never at apex.
Health checks: endpoint (30 s default, 10 s fast), calculated (parent of children), CloudWatch alarm (for PRIVATE resources). Checkers are public -> private endpoints need the alarm type.
Hybrid DNS: Resolver inbound endpoint (on-prem -> VPC names), outbound endpoint + forwarding rules (VPC -> on-prem names).
DR ladder (cost up, RTO/RPO down): Backup & Restore (hours/hours, cheapest, AWS Backup + cross-Region copy) -> Pilot Light (data live e.g. replicated DB, compute off; RPO minutes, RTO 10s of min) -> Warm Standby (scaled-down full stack running; RPO seconds, RTO minutes) -> Multi-site active/active (full stack both Regions, Route 53 latency/weighted; RPO ~0, RTO ~0).
RPO = data you can lose; RTO = downtime you can tolerate.

tier_s_must_memorize_cold.topic: SG vs NACL + VPC endpoints + NAT
tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact:
Security group: instance/ENI level, STATEFUL (return traffic auto-allowed), ALLOW rules only, all rules evaluated, default deny all inbound / allow all outbound, can reference other SGs (same Region incl. peered VPC).
NACL: subnet level, STATELESS (must allow ephemeral 1024-65535 for return traffic), ALLOW + DENY, rules evaluated lowest number first, first match wins; default NACL allows all, custom NACL denies all. Use NACL to block a specific IP.
Gateway endpoint: S3 + DynamoDB ONLY, route-table entry, FREE, same Region, not reachable from on-prem/peered VPC. Interface endpoint (PrivateLink): ENI with private IP, ~all services incl. S3, $0.01/h per AZ + per GB, reachable over DX/VPN, private DNS. Endpoint policy restricts what the endpoint can reach; bucket policy aws:sourceVpce locks S3 to the endpoint.
NAT gateway: managed, lives in ONE AZ (one per AZ for HA), 5-100 Gbps, no SG, $/hour + $/GB processed, needs Elastic IP, in public subnet; private subnet route 0.0.0.0/0 -> NAT GW. NAT instance: EC2, disable source/dest check, has SG, cheaper, you patch it. Egress-only IGW = IPv6 outbound.
Bastion -> replace with SSM Session Manager (no inbound ports, IAM, logged). IMDSv2 (session token, hop limit) defeats SSRF credential theft.
VPC Flow Logs -> CloudWatch Logs / S3 / Firehose; captures ACCEPT/REJECT metadata, not payload; misses DNS to AmazonProvidedDNS, DHCP, metadata traffic.

Policy types: identity-based (grants), resource-based (grants, enables cross-account without AssumeRole; S3/SQS/KMS/Lambda/Secrets), permission boundary (CAPS one principal, grants nothing), SCP (CAPS every identity incl. root in member accounts; no effect on management account; grants nothing), session policy (caps an AssumeRole session). Effective = intersection; explicit Deny always wins.
Cross-account: resource policy + caller identity policy, OR AssumeRole into a role that trusts the account. STS creds 15 min-12 h (role chaining max 1 h). SAML 2.0 IdP -> AssumeRoleWithSAML; OIDC (Google/Cognito) -> AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. Workforce SSO -> IAM Identity Center permission sets. Cognito user pool = authentication (JWT, sign-up, MFA, social/SAML); identity pool = authorization (temp AWS creds, guest access).
Organizations: consolidated billing (RI/SP sharing, volume tiers), OUs, SCPs, tag/backup policies; aws:PrincipalOrgID condition. Control Tower = landing zone + guardrails (preventive = SCP, detective = Config) + Account Factory.
KMS keys: AWS-owned (free, invisible), AWS-managed aws/<service> (free, auto-rotate yearly, no policy control), customer-managed ($1/mo, key policy + grants, optional yearly automatic rotation for symmetric only, cross-account, imported material = no auto rotation), multi-Region keys (same ID, DR/Global tables), asymmetric (sign/verify, no auto rotation). Envelope encryption via GenerateDataKey; direct Encrypt limited to 4 KB. Deletion waiting period 7-30 days. Regional service.
CloudHSM = single-tenant FIPS 140-2 Level 3, you own keys, Oracle TDE/SSL offload, KMS custom key store.
S3 SSE: SSE-S3 (default, free, no audit), SSE-KMS (CloudTrail audit, per-key access control, KMS API quota -> S3 Bucket Keys), DSSE-KMS (two layers), SSE-C (you send the key, HTTPS only), client-side. Secrets Manager rotates (native RDS/Redshift/DocumentDB), $0.40/secret; Parameter Store free standard tier, SecureString via KMS, no native rotation. ACM public certs free + auto-renew, not exportable; CloudFront cert must be in us-east-1.

On-Demand: no commitment, per-second billing (60 s min), spiky/unpredictable/short.
Standard RI: 1 or 3 yr, up to 72%, locked to instance FAMILY (size flex within family for Linux default tenancy, AZ change OK), sellable on RI Marketplace. Convertible RI: up to 66%, can change family/OS/tenancy, not sellable. Payment: All upfront > Partial > No upfront discount. Zonal RI reserves capacity; Regional RI does not.
Savings Plans: Compute SP up to 66%, $/hour commit, any family/size/Region/OS/tenancy, covers EC2 + Fargate + Lambda. EC2 Instance SP up to 72%, locked to family + Region. Default answer for steady compute unless capacity reservation or marketplace resale needed.
Spot: up to 90% off, 2-minute interruption warning, stateless/fault-tolerant/batch/CI/big data/containers; Spot Fleet + capacity rebalancing; NEVER for stateful DBs or must-finish jobs. Spot blocks retired.
Dedicated Host: physical server visible sockets/cores -> BYOL per-socket/per-core licenses (Windows Server, SQL Server), host affinity, compliance; can be reserved. Dedicated Instance: hardware isolated to your account but no socket visibility, may share host with your other instances. Capacity Reservation: guarantees AZ capacity any duration, On-Demand price (no discount) -> stack with RI/SP for discount.
RDS/ElastiCache/Redshift/OpenSearch/DynamoDB have their own reserved pricing (SPs do not cover them).

ALB = L7 HTTP/HTTPS/gRPC/WebSocket; route by path, host, header, query, method, source IP; targets instances/IPs/Lambda/another ALB (or on-prem IPs); fixed-response/redirect; sticky cookies; SNI multi-cert; Cognito/OIDC auth; WAF; X-Forwarded-For; NO static IP (front with NLB or Global Accelerator); cross-zone always on and free.
NLB = L4 TCP/UDP/TLS, millions rps, ultra-low latency, ONE static/Elastic IP per AZ, preserves source IP, TLS termination, PrivateLink endpoint service target, targets incl. ALB; cross-zone off by default.
GWLB = L3 transparent bump-in-the-wire for 3rd-party appliances (firewall/IDS/IPS), GENEVE 6081, GWLB endpoint. CLB = legacy, avoid.
Deregistration delay (draining) default 300 s. ELB health check for ASG = app-level (default EC2 check only catches hardware). Deletion protection.
ASG: launch TEMPLATE (versioned, mixed instances/Spot) not launch configuration; min/desired/max; health check grace 300 s; default cooldown 300 s; lifecycle hooks (pending:wait for bootstrap, terminating:wait for log drain); termination policy default = AZ with most instances -> oldest launch template -> closest to billing hour; scale-in protection; instance refresh; warm pools.
Policies: Target tracking (keep metric at value: CPU 40%, ALBRequestCountPerTarget, SQS backlog per instance custom metric) = default pick. Step scaling (alarm breach bands, add +2/+4). Simple scaling (one adjustment then cooldown; legacy). Scheduled (known peaks, e.g. 9am). Predictive (ML on 14 days of history, pre-provisions; combine with target tracking).
Spread across AZs: ASG rebalances; scale out then in; a stopped instance is unhealthy -> replaced.

tier_s_must_memorize_cold.topic: CloudFront vs Global Accelerator + DX vs VPN vs TGW vs peering vs PrivateLink
tier_s_must_memorize_cold.fact:
CloudFront = CDN, CACHES HTTP(S) content at 600+ PoPs; origins S3/ALB/EC2/any HTTP; OAC locks S3 to CloudFront (replaces OAI, supports SSE-KMS); geo restriction; signed URL (one file) vs signed cookie (many files, no URL change); field-level encryption; TTL default 24 h; invalidations; origin groups failover; WAF + Shield; Price Classes cut cost; S3 -> CloudFront origin fetch free.
Global Accelerator = 2 static anycast IPs, L4 TCP/UDP, NO caching, routes over AWS backbone to nearest healthy ALB/NLB/EC2/EIP in any Region, failover <1 min, deterministic; pick for non-HTTP, gaming/VoIP/IoT, IP allow-listing, multi-Region ALB static IP.
VPC peering = 1:1, NON-transitive, no overlapping CIDRs, cross-account/Region, SG cross-reference same Region.
Transit Gateway = regional hub, TRANSITIVE, up to 5,000 attachments, route tables for segmentation, inter-Region peering, multicast, VPN ECMP, DX via transit VIF; $/attachment-hour + $/GB.
PrivateLink (interface endpoint / endpoint service) = expose ONE service via NLB/GWLB to thousands of consumer VPCs, one-directional, overlapping CIDRs fine, no IGW/NAT/peering.
Direct Connect = private dedicated 1/10/100 Gbps (hosted 50 Mbps-10 Gbps), consistent latency, cheaper egress, weeks to months lead time, NOT encrypted by default (IPsec VPN over DX or MACsec); VIFs: private (VPC), public (S3/DynamoDB public endpoints), transit (DX Gateway -> TGW); DX Gateway spans Regions/accounts; resilience = 2 connections at 2 locations or VPN backup.
Site-to-Site VPN = IPsec over internet, 2 tunnels, 1.25 Gbps/tunnel, minutes to deploy, VGW or TGW target, Accelerated VPN via Global Accelerator, ECMP on TGW to aggregate. Client VPN = OpenVPN users -> VPC. VPN CloudHub = branch offices hub-spoke over VGW.

Cost Explorer = visualize + 13 months history + 12-month forecast + RI/SP purchase recommendations + rightsizing. Budgets = ALERT (cost, usage, RI/SP utilization & coverage) + Budget Actions (apply IAM/SCP, stop EC2/RDS). CUR = most granular raw line items to S3 -> Athena/QuickSight. Cost Anomaly Detection = ML alerts, free. Compute Optimizer = ML right-sizing for EC2/ASG/EBS/Lambda/ECS Fargate (14-day lookback). Trusted Advisor = best-practice checks in cost/performance/security/fault tolerance/service quotas/operational excellence; full checks need Business+ support. Cost allocation tags must be ACTIVATED. Consolidated billing pools volume tiers + shares RI/SP.
Data transfer: inbound free. Out to internet ~$0.09/GB (100 GB/mo free). Inter-Region ~$0.02/GB. Inter-AZ $0.01/GB EACH direction. Same-AZ via PRIVATE IP free; via public/Elastic IP is charged as Regional transfer. Public IPv4 $0.005/h each. S3 -> EC2 same Region free. S3 -> CloudFront free; CloudFront egress cheaper than S3/EC2 egress.
NAT gateway = $0.045/h + $0.045/GB processed -> route S3/DynamoDB through a FREE gateway endpoint instead. Interface endpoint $0.01/h/AZ + $0.01/GB. TGW $0.05/h/attachment + $0.02/GB (peering cheaper for 2 VPCs). DX egress ~$0.02/GB (cheaper than internet).
S3: requests cost; IA/Glacier charge per-GB retrieval; lifecycle transitions charge per 1,000 objects (millions of tiny objects -> aggregate or leave in Standard; IT does not tier <128 KB). Glacier early-delete fees within min duration.
Compute: Graviton ~20-40% cheaper per perf; Spot 90%; SP over RI; Fargate for spiky, EC2 for steady dense; Lambda = requests + GB-s. Aurora I/O-Optimized when I/O >25% of Aurora bill. S3 Requester Pays. Reserved nodes for RDS/ElastiCache/Redshift/OpenSearch.

D1.fact: Explicit Deny > SCP > resource policy > permission boundary > session policy > identity policy. Default is implicit deny. Effective permissions = intersection of identity policy with each cap (SCP, boundary, session).

SCPs cap member-account identities including root; never affect the management account; never grant. Service-linked roles are exempt. Deny-list strategy (FullAWSAccess + deny statements) is the default and recommended.
Managed policy attached to a user/role setting its MAX permissions. Classic use: let developers create roles but only within the boundary (iam:PermissionsBoundary condition on iam:CreateRole).

Resource policy keeps the caller's own identity and lets them still access their own account resources in the same call; AssumeRole swaps identity. Services supporting resource policies: S3, SQS, SNS, KMS, Lambda, Secrets Manager, ECR, API Gateway, EventBridge, Glue.

D1.topic: IAM roles for EC2 / Lambda / ECS
D1.fact: Never store access keys on instances; attach an instance profile role. ECS task role (per task) vs container instance role (agent). Lambda execution role. Roles rotate creds automatically via IMDS.

Enterprise AD/SAML -> IAM Identity Center (multi-account) or SAML 2.0 role federation; web/mobile users -> Cognito user pool (authn) + identity pool (temp creds); Active Directory on AWS -> AWS Managed Microsoft AD (trust with on-prem), AD Connector (proxy, no cache), Simple AD (standalone Samba, small).
Root: enable MFA, no access keys, use only for account tasks. Enforce MFA via aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent condition. S3 MFA Delete requires root + CLI + versioning.

Bucket policy (resource, cross-account, aws:SecureTransport / aws:sourceVpce / aws:PrincipalOrgID conditions) > IAM policy > ACL (disable ACLs with Bucket owner enforced). Block Public Access at account level. Access Points simplify shared buckets (per-app policies, VPC-only). Pre-signed URLs delegate temporary access (max 7 days).

Bucket policy Deny PutObject unless s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption = aws:kms (or AES256). Default encryption applies SSE-S3 automatically since 2023. Deny when aws:SecureTransport is false to force TLS. SSE-KMS gives CloudTrail audit + per-key control; S3 Bucket Keys reduce KMS request cost.

D1.topic: S3 Object Lock and Vault Lock
D1.fact: Object Lock needs versioning. Governance mode: privileged users (s3:BypassGovernanceRetention) can delete/shorten. Compliance mode: nobody including root until retention ends. Legal hold = indefinite, independent of retention. Glacier Vault Lock = immutable vault policy (legacy vaults). AWS Backup Vault Lock = WORM backups.

Key policy is mandatory and is the primary access control; IAM policies work only if the key policy delegates to the account. Grants = temporary programmatic permissions (used by AWS services). Cross-account: key policy allows external account + their IAM policy allows kms actions. Imported key material and asymmetric keys cannot auto-rotate.

Secrets Manager: automatic rotation (Lambda, native RDS/Aurora/Redshift/DocumentDB), cross-Region replication, resource policy, $0.40/secret/mo + API. Parameter Store: free standard tier (4 KB, 10k params), advanced ($0.05, 8 KB, parameter policies), hierarchies, SecureString via KMS, no native rotation, integrates with CloudFormation dynamic refs.

WAF (L7 rules: SQLi/XSS, IP sets, geo, rate-based, managed rule groups, Bot Control, CAPTCHA) attaches to CloudFront/ALB/API GW/AppSync/Cognito, NOT NLB. Shield Standard free L3/L4 always-on. Shield Advanced $3k/mo: L7 DDoS, SRT 24x7, cost protection, protects EC2/ELB/CloudFront/GA/Route 53. Firewall Manager pushes WAF/Shield/SG/Network Firewall policies org-wide.

GuardDuty = threat detection (ML on CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, EKS audit, S3 data events, RDS logins, Malware Protection), one click, findings -> EventBridge. Inspector = vulnerability/CVE + network reachability scans of EC2 (SSM agent), ECR images, Lambda. Macie = PII/sensitive data discovery in S3. Detective = investigate root cause graph after GuardDuty findings. Security Hub = aggregate findings + CSPM standards (CIS, PCI, FSBP), needs Config.

Config = WHAT does a resource look like / is it compliant (rules, history, remediation via SSM Automation, conformance packs). CloudTrail = WHO called WHICH API (90-day event history free; trail to S3 for retention, org trail, data events extra, log file validation, Insights). CloudWatch = metrics, logs, alarms, dashboards (performance).

D1.topic: Network Firewall vs NACL/SG vs WAF
D1.fact: Network Firewall = managed stateful/stateless L3-L7 VPC firewall with Suricata rules, domain filtering, IDS/IPS, deployed per AZ via firewall endpoints in an inspection subnet; centrally managed by Firewall Manager. SG/NACL = simple allow/deny by IP/port. WAF = HTTP request content. Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall = block DNS lookups to bad domains.

Gateway endpoints: S3 + DynamoDB, free, route table. Interface endpoints: everything else (and S3), PrivateLink, DNS names. Endpoint policy restricts actions. On-prem over DX/VPN can use interface endpoints only. API Gateway private endpoint = REST API reachable only from VPC via interface endpoint + resource policy.

SSM Session Manager: no SSH port, no bastion, IAM-controlled, session logs to S3/CloudWatch; needs SSM agent + instance role + outbound to SSM endpoints (or interface endpoints). EC2 Instance Connect = temporary SSH keys via API. IMDSv2 enforced in launch template (HttpTokens=required).

ACM public certs free, auto-renew, usable on ELB/CloudFront/API GW/App Runner; cannot install on EC2 or export (use ACM Private CA or import). CloudFront requires the cert in us-east-1. NLB TLS listener terminates TLS; ALB HTTPS listener with SNI for multiple domains. End-to-end encryption = re-encrypt at target (self-signed OK on backend).

AWS Artifact = download SOC/PCI/ISO reports and accept agreements (BAA). Audit Manager = continuous evidence collection against frameworks. Shared responsibility: AWS secures OF the cloud (hardware, managed service patching), customer secures IN the cloud (data, IAM, OS on EC2, SG rules).

D2.fact: RPO = max acceptable data loss (time between last backup/replica and failure). RTO = max acceptable downtime. Availability 99.99% = 52 min/yr. Multi-AZ = survive AZ loss; multi-Region = survive Region loss. Stateless tiers + externalized state (S3, DynamoDB, ElastiCache sessions) enable horizontal scaling and self-healing.

ALB/NLB spans AZs; ASG across >=2 AZs (3 preferred); RDS Multi-AZ; Aurora 3 AZs; ElastiCache Redis Multi-AZ with auto failover (Memcached has none); EFS Regional; NAT gateway per AZ (a single NAT GW is a cross-AZ single point of failure); interface endpoint ENI per AZ; DynamoDB/S3/SQS are multi-AZ by design.

Multi-AZ failover flips the DNS CNAME to the standby (apps must reconnect/not cache DNS); triggers: AZ outage, primary failure, instance type change, OS patching, manual reboot with failover. Read replica promotion is MANUAL and breaks replication. Multi-AZ cluster gives readable standbys + faster failover.

Replicas are failover targets (tier 0-15; same-size preferred); no replica -> Aurora recreates the instance (slower). Reader endpoint load balances; custom endpoints group replicas (analytics vs OLTP). Global Database: managed planned failover (RPO 0) vs unplanned detach-and-promote (RPO ~1 s); write forwarding from secondaries. Backtrack (MySQL) vs PITR vs clone.
Global tables active-active multi-Region (replicated within ~1 s), PITR 35 days, on-demand backups, Streams + Lambda for reacting to changes, DAX Multi-AZ clusters. Conflict = last writer wins.

Versioning protects against overwrite/delete (delete marker); MFA Delete; CRR (cross-Region, needs versioning both sides, new objects only unless Batch Replication, RTC 15-min SLA, optional delete-marker replication) for DR/compliance/latency; SRR for log aggregation/prod->test. Object Lock for immutability. Multi-Region Access Points route to nearest bucket.

Volume is single-AZ; snapshots (incremental, S3, cross-Region/account copy), Fast Snapshot Restore removes first-read latency, Data Lifecycle Manager schedules snapshots, Recycle Bin recovers deleted snapshots/AMIs. To move an instance to another AZ: snapshot -> volume in new AZ / AMI -> launch.

Put SQS between tiers so consumers can fail/scale independently; DLQ isolates poison messages after maxReceiveCount; visibility timeout >= processing time (or extend via ChangeMessageVisibility); idempotent consumers for Standard's at-least-once. SNS fan-out to multiple SQS queues so each consumer has its own durable copy.

Failover routing + health check on primary (secondary can be an S3 static maintenance page via alias). Multi-Region active-active: latency or weighted with health checks. Health checks cannot reach private IPs -> use CloudWatch alarm health checks. Evaluate Target Health for alias records to ELB.

Backup/restore: hours RTO, cheapest, AWS Backup + cross-Region copy + CloudFormation to rebuild. Pilot light: DB replicated (read replica / Aurora Global / DMS), servers as AMIs, ASG at 0, RTO tens of minutes. Warm standby: scaled-down copy serving no/low traffic, RTO minutes, scale out on failover. Multi-site: full capacity both sides, RTO ~0. Elastic Disaster Recovery (DRS) = block-level continuous replication for lift-and-shift servers with pilot-light cost.

Central policy-based backup across EBS, EC2, RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, EFS, FSx, Storage Gateway, S3, DocumentDB, Neptune, Redshift, VMware; backup plans with lifecycle to cold storage; cross-Region and cross-account copy; Backup Vault Lock (WORM); Organizations backup policies; Audit Manager for compliance reports.

Use ELB health checks so app-level failures replace instances; grace period covers boot; lifecycle hooks to drain logs; instance refresh for AMI rollouts; capacity rebalancing for Spot; warm pools for slow-boot apps; Standby state for debugging without termination; scale-in protection for in-flight work.

Store sessions in ElastiCache Redis (Multi-AZ) or DynamoDB, not on the instance; ALB sticky sessions are a fallback that hurts balance. Uploads go to S3, not local disk. Shared config in Parameter Store/AppConfig.

ECS service scheduler keeps desired count and spreads tasks across AZs; Fargate removes host failures; Lambda is multi-AZ by default; Lambda async retries 2x then DLQ/destination; SQS event source with partial batch responses; Step Functions Retry/Catch for workflow error handling; API Gateway throttling protects backends.

Volume Gateway stored mode keeps full data on-prem with async EBS snapshots for DR; cached mode keeps primary in S3 (needs network). File Gateway caches recent data. Tape Gateway replaces physical tape libraries with S3/Glacier. On-prem outage -> restore Volume Gateway snapshots as EBS volumes in AWS.

Nitro-based for ENA/EFA.

Cluster = one AZ, low latency/high throughput (HPC, EFA), same instance type, launch all at once. Spread = distinct racks, max 7 instances per AZ per group, critical instances. Partition = groups of racks, up to 7 partitions per AZ, hundreds of instances, HDFS/HBase/Cassandra/Kafka aware of topology.

Enhanced networking (ENA/SR-IOV) up to 100 Gbps; EFA for MPI/HPC OS-bypass (only in cluster PG); Elastic Network Interfaces for multi-homing; jumbo frames within VPC. Hibernate persists RAM to encrypted EBS root (<150 GB RAM, <=60 days).

gp3: pick when you need IOPS/throughput without paying for size (3k/125 baseline, up to 16k/1,000). io2 Block Express for >16k IOPS or sub-ms (up to 256k, 4,000 MB/s). st1 for sequential big data/logs (500 MB/s), sc1 cheapest cold. EBS-optimized instances give dedicated EBS bandwidth. RAID 0 to stripe for IOPS; RAID 1 is redundant (rarely needed). Initialize volumes restored from snapshots (or FSR).

Elastic throughput (default for spiky/unknown), Bursting (scales with size), Provisioned (fixed MB/s independent of size). General Purpose mode (lowest latency, up to 35k IOPS... default) vs Max I/O (higher aggregate, higher latency, not with Elastic). EFS IA + lifecycle (7-90 days) cuts cost; One Zone for non-critical. Access Points for per-app roots.

Windows/SMB/AD/NTFS/DFS -> FSx for Windows. HPC/ML/media, S3-backed, 100s GB/s -> FSx for Lustre (scratch = temp cheap; persistent = long-lived, replicated). NetApp/multi-protocol/iSCSI/SnapMirror -> FSx for ONTAP. ZFS/Linux NFS, snapshots/clones, 1M IOPS -> FSx for OpenZFS.

3,500 PUT/COPY/POST/DELETE and 5,500 GET/HEAD per prefix per second, unlimited prefixes -> spread keys across prefixes. Multipart upload (>100 MB recommended, mandatory >5 GB; 5 TB max object). Byte-range fetches parallelize downloads. Transfer Acceleration for long-distance uploads via edge. S3 Select / Glacier Select filter server-side with SQL. Strong read-after-write consistency. Express One Zone: single-digit ms, directory buckets.

CloudFront (edge, static + dynamic HTTP); API Gateway cache (0.5-237 GB, TTL 300 s default); ElastiCache in front of RDS (lazy loading vs write-through, TTL); DAX in front of DynamoDB; Redis for sessions/leaderboards/pub-sub/geospatial; Memcached for simple multi-threaded object cache with no persistence; Aurora read replicas for read scaling; Route 53 TTL for DNS caching.

Redis: replication, Multi-AZ auto failover, persistence/snapshots, sorted sets, pub/sub, Lua, geospatial, cluster mode sharding, Global Datastore cross-Region, AUTH/IAM, encryption. Memcached: multi-threaded, simple key-value, horizontal partitioning, no replication/persistence/failover. MemoryDB = Redis-compatible DURABLE primary database (Multi-AZ transaction log).

Relational OLTP -> RDS (managed engines) or Aurora (5x MySQL / 3x PG, HA, serverless). Key-value at scale -> DynamoDB. Graph -> Neptune. MongoDB -> DocumentDB. Cassandra -> Keyspaces. Time series/IoT -> Timestream. Immutable ledger -> QLDB (centralized; Managed Blockchain is decentralized). Search/logs -> OpenSearch. OLAP DW -> Redshift. Ad hoc SQL on S3 -> Athena. In-memory -> ElastiCache/MemoryDB.

Read replicas offload reads (async lag); RDS Proxy pools connections (Lambda, failover); gp3/io1 storage with Provisioned IOPS; Performance Insights + Enhanced Monitoring (OS metrics via agent); storage autoscaling; scale vertically with brief downtime (or on Multi-AZ failover); Aurora Serverless v2 for variable load; Aurora parallel query for analytics.

Columnar MPP; RA3 nodes separate compute from managed storage (scale independently); Redshift Spectrum queries S3 in place (needs a cluster); Serverless for sporadic; distribution/sort keys; Concurrency Scaling; zero-ETL from Aurora; snapshots to S3 and cross-Region; single-AZ by default (Multi-AZ now available for RA3). Not for OLTP.

Serverless SQL on S3 -> Athena (partition + Parquet + compress to cut $/TB). Serverless ETL + catalog + crawlers -> Glue (DataBrew for visual prep). Spark/Hadoop/Presto control, Spot task nodes -> EMR. Real-time stream SQL/Flink -> Managed Service for Apache Flink. BI dashboards -> QuickSight (SPICE). Data-lake permissions (column/row) -> Lake Formation. Search/log analytics -> OpenSearch. Kafka -> MSK. Orchestration -> Step Functions / MWAA (Airflow).

Real-time with replay/multiple consumers -> Kinesis Data Streams. Just land the stream in S3/Redshift/OpenSearch with zero admin -> Firehose. Buffer work for one consumer group -> SQS. Event routing/SaaS/schedules -> EventBridge. SaaS -> S3/Redshift bulk (Salesforce, SAP) -> AppFlow. Bulk file/NFS/SMB -> DataSync. Database migration/CDC -> DMS.

Memory 128 MB-10 GB drives CPU (6 vCPU at 10 GB) -> raise memory to speed CPU-bound code. 15-min timeout, 6 MB sync / 256 KB async payload, 10 GB /tmp, 50 MB zip / 250 MB unzipped / 10 GB image, 1,000 concurrency default. Provisioned concurrency kills cold starts (SnapStart for Java); reserved concurrency caps/guarantees. VPC Lambda needs NAT/endpoints for internet/AWS APIs. EFS mount for shared files. Event source: SQS batch up to 10,000, Kinesis/DynamoDB Streams per shard, batch window.

REST API: API keys + usage plans, request validation, caching, WAF, resource policies, private endpoints, canary, Lambda/Cognito/IAM authorizers, edge-optimized/regional/private; 29 s integration timeout; 10 MB payload; 10,000 rps + 5,000 burst default. HTTP API: ~70% cheaper, lower latency, JWT/OIDC authorizer, no caching/usage plans/WAF/request validation. WebSocket API: bidirectional (chat, live dashboards). AppSync = managed GraphQL with real-time subscriptions and offline sync.

ECS on EC2 = you own capacity (steady dense workloads, GPU, custom AMIs, reserved pricing). Fargate = serverless tasks (no host management, per vCPU/GB-second, awsvpc). EKS = Kubernetes portability/existing manifests. App Runner = simplest container/source web app. ECS task role for per-task IAM; ALB dynamic port mapping; ECR with image scanning + lifecycle policies; ECS Anywhere/EKS Anywhere for on-prem.

CloudFront caches HTTP at edge and terminates TLS close to users; Global Accelerator gives static anycast IPs + backbone routing for TCP/UDP; Route 53 latency routing picks the closest Region; Aurora Global / DynamoDB global tables for local reads; S3 Transfer Acceleration for uploads; Local Zones / Wavelength / Outposts for single-digit-ms edge compute; Lambda@Edge / CloudFront Functions for edge logic.

Lambda@Edge: Node/Python, all 4 events (viewer + origin), up to 5 s viewer / 30 s origin, network + body access -> A/B, origin selection, auth calls, image resize.

Watch min durations (30/30/90/90/180) and 128 KB min billable size, per-GB retrieval fees for IA/Glacier, transition request charges for millions of tiny objects. Express One Zone costs more per GB but less per request for hot data. Storage Lens + S3 Inventory find waste; Intelligent-Tiering for unknown patterns; lifecycle expiration for logs.

gp3 ~20% cheaper than gp2 at same size and lets you buy IOPS separately; sc1 cheapest for cold sequential; delete unattached volumes and stale snapshots (Data Lifecycle Manager retention); snapshots archive tier (75% cheaper, 24-72 h restore, 90-day min); Instance store is free with the instance.

EFS IA + Archive with lifecycle (files not accessed in N days); EFS One Zone ~47% cheaper; Elastic throughput avoids over-provisioning; FSx Lustre scratch cheaper than persistent; FSx ONTAP dedup/compression + capacity pool tier; FSx Windows HDD storage for cold shares.

Reserved instances for RDS/ElastiCache/Redshift/OpenSearch (1-3 yr). Aurora Serverless v2 for variable; Aurora I/O-Optimized when I/O >25% of bill; RDS stop instances (7 days max, auto restart) for dev; Multi-AZ doubles cost -> only for prod. DynamoDB: provisioned + auto scaling for steady, on-demand for spiky, Standard-IA table class for cold, TTL to free storage, reserved capacity for steady baseline. Redshift pause/resume + Serverless; Spectrum/Athena to avoid loading cold data.

Inbound free; egress to internet ~$0.09/GB (100 GB free); inter-Region ~$0.02; inter-AZ $0.01 each way; same-AZ private IP free; public IP traffic within Region is charged; CloudFront egress cheaper than S3/EC2 egress and S3 -> CloudFront free; DX egress ~$0.02 vs $0.09 internet; VPC peering same-AZ free; TGW adds per-GB + per-attachment fees.

$0.045/h + $0.045/GB processed per NAT GW. Private subnets talking to S3/DynamoDB -> gateway endpoint (free) and skip NAT. Heavy AWS API traffic -> interface endpoints ($0.01/GB) cheaper than NAT ($0.045/GB). One NAT GW per AZ costs more but avoids cross-AZ transfer + SPOF; dev can share one.

Lambda = requests + GB-seconds (1M requests + 400k GB-s free/mo); tune memory (faster may be cheaper); Compute Savings Plans cover Lambda; provisioned concurrency costs even idle. API Gateway HTTP API ~$1/M vs REST ~$3.50/M. Step Functions Standard per state transition vs Express per request+duration (Express cheaper for high volume short). Fargate Spot up to 70% off; Fargate per-second billing.

Cost Explorer (analyze, forecast, RI/SP recommendations) vs Budgets (alerts + actions) vs Cost & Usage Report (raw hourly line items to S3, query with Athena) vs Cost Anomaly Detection (ML alerts) vs Billing Conductor (custom rates for chargeback) vs Pricing Calculator (pre-deployment estimate). Cost allocation tags (activate!) + Cost Categories for chargeback. Split cost allocation data for ECS/EKS.

Consolidated billing: one bill, volume tiers pooled (S3, data transfer), RI/SP discounts shared across accounts (can be disabled per account), free. Compute Optimizer + Trusted Advisor org-wide. Service Control Policies to block expensive Regions/services. Budgets per account/OU.

Basic (free, TA core checks), Developer ($29+, business hours email), Business ($100+ min, 24x7 phone/chat, full Trusted Advisor, 1-h production-down response, IEM extra), Enterprise On-Ramp ($5.5k, 30-min business-critical), Enterprise ($15k, TAM, 15-min business-critical, concierge).

Transfer time = size / bandwidth: 1 Gbps ~ 10 TB/day; 100 TB @ 1 Gbps ~ 10-12 days. If > ~1 week or link is saturated by production -> Snowball Edge (80 TB, ~$300/job + $/day after 10 days). DataSync charges per GB but uses your DX/internet. Snowball into S3 Standard then lifecycle to Glacier (cannot import directly to Glacier).

GET/PUT charged per 1,000; Glacier retrieval per GB by tier (Bulk cheapest, Expedited priciest); Deep Archive restore 12-48 h; Standard-IA retrieval $0.01/GB -> frequently re-read data belongs in Standard; Intelligent-Tiering has no retrieval fee but $0.0025/1,000 objects monitoring; Requester Pays pushes transfer cost to downloader.

CloudFront reduces origin egress + compute; ElastiCache/DAX reduce DB instance size or RCUs; API Gateway caching reduces Lambda invocations; S3 static hosting + CloudFront replaces web servers; Route 53 alias records are free queries.

BYOL per-socket/per-core (Windows Server, SQL Server Enterprise, Oracle) -> Dedicated Hosts (+ License Manager). License-included RDS vs BYOL for Oracle. SQL Server Web edition cheaper. Dedicated Instances cost more than default tenancy but do not enable socket-based BYOL.

Serverless for spiky/low-duty (Lambda, Fargate, Aurora Serverless, DynamoDB on-demand, Athena). Managed beats self-managed on TCO. Spot for batch/EMR task nodes/CI. Static content -> S3 + CloudFront. Logs -> S3 + lifecycle + Athena, not a DB. Stop non-prod at night (Instance Scheduler). Delete idle: EIPs, unattached EBS, old snapshots, idle ELBs, idle NAT GWs.

Gateway endpoints, VPC peering same-AZ transfer, inbound data transfer, S3 -> CloudFront, ACM public certs, Shield Standard, Cost Anomaly Detection, CloudTrail 90-day event history + one management trail, first 2 Budgets, Compute Optimizer, IAM/Organizations/Control Tower (pay for resources), CloudWatch basic metrics, Trusted Advisor core checks.

mnemonics.hook: Backup -> Pilot light -> Warm standby -> Multi-site: Cost goes UP, RTO comes DOWN

mnemonics.expands_to: Standard 0, Intelligent-Tiering 0, Standard-IA 30, One Zone-IA 30, Glacier Instant 90, Glacier Flexible 90, Deep Archive 180

mnemonics.hook: Glacier: Expedited minutes, Standard hours (3-5), Bulk half-day (5-12); Deep = 12/48
mnemonics.expands_to: Glacier Flexible Retrieval tiers 1-5 min / 3-5 h / 5-12 h; Deep Archive Standard 12 h / Bulk 48 h

mnemonics.hook: SG = Stateful Gatekeeper, NACL = No memory (stateless) + Numbered rules
mnemonics.expands_to: Security groups remember return traffic and only allow; NACLs evaluate numbered rules in order, allow and deny, and need ephemeral-port return rules
mnemonics.use_for: any firewall question: block an IP -> NACL deny; instance-level allow -> SG

mnemonics.hook: Gateway endpoints = S3 + DynamoDB only, and they are free

mnemonics.hook: C-compute M-mixed R-RAM I-IOPS P/G-GPU T-tiny/burst X-eXtra memory D-Dense disk
mnemonics.expands_to: EC2 family letters: C compute-optimized, M general purpose, R memory, I storage/NVMe IOPS, P training GPU, G graphics/inference GPU, T burstable, X/u high memory (SAP HANA), D/H dense HDD

mnemonics.hook: Kinesis shard: 1 in, 2 out

mnemonics.hook: RDS backups 35, PITR 35, DynamoDB PITR 35
mnemonics.expands_to: 35 days is the max automated backup retention for RDS/Aurora and the PITR window for DynamoDB

mnemonics.hook: Spot 2-min warning, Spot 90, RI 72, Convertible 66, Compute SP 66, EC2 SP 72

mnemonics.hook: Cluster = Close, Spread = Separate (7 per AZ), Partition = Partitioned racks (7 partitions per AZ)
mnemonics.expands_to: Placement groups: cluster packs in one AZ for low latency; spread puts each instance on distinct hardware max 7/AZ; partition groups instances into up to 7 rack partitions per AZ for Hadoop/Cassandra/Kafka
mnemonics.use_for: 'HPC low latency' vs 'critical instances on separate hardware' vs 'HDFS/Kafka'

mnemonics.hook: Multi-AZ = Availability, Read replica = Reads, Aurora = Both, Global = Region
mnemonics.expands_to: RDS Multi-AZ gives failover not reads; read replicas give reads not failover; Aurora replicas give both; Aurora Global / DynamoDB global tables give cross-Region
mnemonics.use_for: the single most tested RDS discrimination

mnemonics.hook: WHERE (Geolocation) vs HOW FAST (Latency) vs HOW MUCH (Weighted) vs IF DOWN (Failover) vs HOW FAR-ish (Geoproximity bias)
mnemonics.expands_to: Route 53 routing policies mapped to the question they answer

mnemonics.hook: CloudFront Caches Content; Global Accelerator Gives Global IPs
mnemonics.expands_to: CloudFront = HTTP caching CDN; Global Accelerator = 2 static anycast IPs, TCP/UDP, no caching, backbone routing + fast failover

mnemonics.hook: Peering is a Pair; Transit is Transitive; PrivateLink is a Private one-way Link
mnemonics.expands_to: VPC peering 1:1 non-transitive; Transit Gateway hub transitive; PrivateLink exposes one service unidirectionally and tolerates overlapping CIDRs

mnemonics.hook: DX is Dedicated but not Defended (encrypt it yourself)
mnemonics.expands_to: Direct Connect is private and consistent but not encrypted by default -> VPN over DX or MACsec
mnemonics.use_for: 'private AND encrypted connection' -> DX + IPsec VPN

mnemonics.hook: SCP and Boundaries are CEILINGS, not floors
mnemonics.expands_to: Service control policies and permission boundaries only cap permissions; a matching identity policy must still grant them
mnemonics.use_for: 'user has AdministratorAccess but cannot do X' -> look for SCP/boundary/explicit deny

mnemonics.hook: KMS: S3 = simple, KMS = kept logs, C = customer carries the key

mnemonics.hook: Secrets Manager SPINS (rotates); Parameter Store STORES
mnemonics.expands_to: Secrets Manager has native automatic rotation and costs per secret; Parameter Store is free for config/SecureStrings but does not rotate natively

mnemonics.hook: Config = Compliance/Configuration, CloudTrail = Calls (who), CloudWatch = Watch metrics
mnemonics.expands_to: Three C services: Config tracks resource state and compliance; CloudTrail records API calls; CloudWatch handles metrics/logs/alarms

mnemonics.hook: Streams Store (replay), Firehose Flows (deliver)

mnemonics.use_for: 'multiple consumers / replay' vs 'just load it into S3'

mnemonics.hook: Cached = Cloud is primary (hot subset local); Stored = Site is primary (async snapshots to cloud)

mnemonics.hook: 1 Gbps ~ 10 TB/day
mnemonics.expands_to: 125 MB/s x 86,400 s ~ 10.8 TB per day; 100 TB over 1 Gbps ~ 10 days -> Snowball territory

mnemonics.hook: ALB = Application (L7 paths), NLB = Network (L4 static IP), GWLB = Gateway to appliances

mnemonics.hook: LEAST operational overhead = most managed / serverless
